query: Our team calls a long system prompt the agent's safety boundary. Design a layered control matrix covering proposals, permissions, execution, output, budgets, and meaningful approval with explicit enforcement owners.

Compose safety and quality checks for a support assistant with harmless reads and consequential updates. Choose proportional controls and define abstention, denial, and partial results when required checks fail.
A content classifier allows an action that the policy engine denies. Specify precedence, failure handling, and tests for contradictory layers so probabilistic scores cannot bypass hard constraints.
Review an agent whose output filter blocks a message only after it has already been sent. Move controls to the right boundaries and verify pre-execution denial and receipt-backed outcome checks.
Design outage behavior when an AI workflow's required checker is unavailable. Fail closed for critical effects, allow policy-approved read-only degradation, and bound repair and escalation loops.

Measure whether optional safety classifiers improve an assistant without excessive false blocking. Define severity-aware thresholds, sandbox ablations, review burden, and latency while preserving mandatory permissions.

Build a risk-to-control matrix for an expense assistant: malformed proposals, stale grants, missing evidence, cumulative budget exhaustion, and unsupported actions. Identify bypass paths across retries and resumed workers.

Our agent can safely refuse, ask for evidence, or request human review, but these paths are inconsistent. Compose validators, policy gates, limits, and escalation rules with concrete terminal behavior.

Evaluate a runtime containment design under poisoned inputs, layer disagreement, expired approval, and legitimate difficult tasks. Assert actual effects and false positives, not just reassuring assistant text.

Design release and rollback checks for layered agent controls. Capture control versions, compatibility, violation rates, abstention, added cost, and an operator path without adding redundant gates everywhere.

Threat-model indirect prompt injection, malicious tool metadata, memory poisoning, credential exfiltration, and confused-deputy execution. Trace attacker-to-effect paths; composing all operational quality controls is outside scope.
Implement a typed admission function for proposed transfers with principal checks, policy version, hard reserve rules, and atomic commit. Existing surrounding guardrail layers are unchanged.
Design an approval interface for external agent actions with exact previews, authorized reviewers, item rejection, expiry, and cancellation. Policy and enforcement composition already exist.
Write a production prompt with clear responsibilities, source-data separation, evidence requirements, and stop conditions. We need a versioned instruction artifact, not a runtime enforcement system.
Validate ordinary form input using allowed fields, length bounds, enums, and consistent errors. No model output, AI runtime, or composed agent control layers are present.
Define a structured model proposal schema with refusal variants, semantic checks, bounded repair, and migration tests. Keep the established authorization and runtime guardrails fixed.
Design unknown-effect reconciliation, checkpoint resume, retry ceilings, compensation, and poison-task handling for an agent. The missing contract is recovery semantics, not layering safety controls.
Build agent runtime tests using production validators, scripted model outputs, provider fakes, and crash injection. The control design is approved; implement verification and CI coverage.

Create representative gold tasks and calibrated rubrics for agent correctness, grounding, abstention, safety, and release regression slices. Evaluate the fixed product rather than redesign containment.
Instrument existing policy decisions, approvals, tool attempts, evaluator results, and terminal statuses with safe correlated events. We need reconstructable trajectories under current controls.
